requirements.requirement: Serve the documentation and purchasing sites from their respective supplied trees using name-based virtual hosting on shared TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct tests before and after restart returned the correct index and supplementary-file content for both hostnames. Listener observations show one nginx service bound to port 8080 on IPv4 and IPv6, and cross-tenant file requests returned 404.

requirements.requirement: Return an error for an unknown Host header rather than serving either tenant's content.
requirements.summary: Requests using unknown.branch.test returned HTTP 404 both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the approved content staged under /srv/legacy2/name-based-web-tenants.
requirements.summary: All five staged files retained SHA-256 hashes identical to the preparation baseline, including after restart. The supplied content was served directly from the staged trees.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. nginx 1.28.3-r7 was installed through Alpine's native package manager, and the lifecycle snapshot confirms the same platform after execution.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart behavior. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged and followed by connection loss, the post-restart boot ID changed, and nginx, both sites, rejection behavior, content hashes, listener state, OS, and kernel were verified recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot transition.
limitations: The Alpine environment does not support the lifecycle collector's systemd failed-unit probe, although direct OpenRC status checks showed nginx running before and after restart.
The lifecycle inventory shows minor temporary evidence artifacts left in /tmp, and there is no final direct inventory confirming cleanup of the nginx rollback copy.
No separate cluster-state probe was applicable because the managed topology contains only one standalone node.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or destructive mutations are evidenced: installing nginx, configuring and enabling it, and restarting the node all directly supported the requested outcome or mandatory restart protocol. Package-health output was unchanged from the pre-executor baseline. Minor residue remained: final evidence shows five small temporary files created by the restart and HTTP verification commands under /tmp. The configuration command also created a rollback copy of the former default configuration, but no final observation establishes whether it was later removed. These are low-risk cleanup shortcomings rather than functional or security defects.
